Route Description: Original description too long. Must be amended to 400 characters or less. Please see WalksinSpain write up for current description.
Directions: Take the CV70 from Guadalest towards Alcoy. Go through Confrides until at approx Km 19.4 find a track off R and park.

Route Name: Les Fonts de Pedreguer, Font d'Aixa, & Camí dels Pouets
Route Description: Good views. Steady climb/descent three times. Worth the effort.
Directions: Parking at Ermita sant blas. On CV720 Alcalali to Pedreguer road at Tourist signs to Ermita at edge of village, turn into Avenida de Maria Lopez and go to the far end of this road (over several junctions) and turn right to park near Ermita beside open ground.
Restrictions: Not Saturdays due to market in Pedreguer
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: Very nice shorter (2 1/2 hrs walking time) walk from 4km behind Font Moli in Finistrat, up to Puig Campana circuit path, continuing up to Collado del Llamp, along the Collado de Sacarest with its impressive views of the Castellets and returning to Realet Dalt. A side trip up Monte Ponoch would add a further hour and increase difficulty from easy to medium.
Directions: From the center crossroads in Finestrat drive N to Font del Moli. From here continue along the â€œmainâ€ surfaced road 3.4 km to a junction. Turn up R. Shortly after (.1 km.) take first turn R. Continue on this road to the end of the paved section (1 km.) This is the start and there is parking for at least 6 cars.

Route Name: Puig Campana East from La Nucia
Route Description: This walk starts in the valleys below the impressive Puig Campana. Then it climbs to link with part of the well known circuit of the Puig Campana but going anti-clockwise reveals different views. Decends again to a valley with grand views of Ponoch, circuits the Tossal del Grau and follows the charming Barranco del Lliriet back to the start.
Directions: Drive south along the CV70 towards Benidorm to KM 44. Immediately after the sign turn R and zero your odometer. Drive along the surfaced road for approx. 0.9 km to a roundabout. Drive straight across to a Y junction. Take the R.H. fork along a track, which is rough in parts, past a casa on your L with blue domed roofs, for a further 2.5 km to where a track goes off down L to a ruin, a total of 3.4 km from the CV70. This junction is the start and end. There is parking for 4/5 cars. Note: After the blue roofed Casa the track up to the start becomes very rough in places but is passable. If it proves too rough for your vehicle there are plenty of spots to pull off, park and walk the rest of the way to the start."

Route Description: The walk follows faint paths on a spectacular ridge before using a marked path into the barranco. The descent is steep and slippery in places. In the barranco we walk downstream through dramatic gorges to reach a dam. We return up the barranco, to reach another dam which we cross using iron rungs and chains. We continue in dramatic landscape to a well defined (but rather worn) path back to the car park.
Directions: Bar “Venta Strambotik” On CV 800 (ex N340) from Campello to Alcoy, km 6.5 . To get there take AP7 to junction with CV 800 and then head towards Alcoy for about 3km. Bar is on right-hand side of road. (This takes only 35 minutes from Altea Junction 64 on AP7) Convoy to start of walk.

Route Description: Rugged paths up the east ridge go across to the ‘Hoyo’. A marked path with (optional cave visit) leads to unmarked paths up the western flank (passing twice through the East/West Meridian) to the summit. Descending the east ridge regains the col crossed earlier. Then down via the ‘Squeeze’ directly to Font D’Aixa. Some terrain is rough and vague. Sometimes a little scratchy. Excellent views.
Directions: This is the junction of CV-748 & Cami Font D'Aixa. At km 5.25 on the Gata to Lliber CV-748, turn north along Cami Font D'Aixa, beside an info board for Escalade (Rock climbing). Follow the narrow Cami for 2.4km (not suitable for large vehicles eg. Motorhomes) to reach the font car park at Lat: 38.766916, Long: 0.019138. (not all sat nav's will find this).
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Ѧ Segaria summit from the East and return via masts Ѧ
Route Description: A very pleasant walk for the main part around this rugged mountain with a tough ascent over rocky ground to the summit. A little scrambling.
Directions: Take the CV729 to Benimeli. In centre of Benimeli turn off the CV729 at brown sign “Pou de Baix”. Park near outdoor piscina.

Route Name: Sella, Castell & Ruta del Aigua Extended
Route Description: A climb up through the charming village to Castle & Ermita. Down to visit various fonts & water features. Via crossings of the Rio's Voltes, l'Arc & Sella. Through delightful countryside, up over a ridge via old mule trails. Mostly straightforward paths & tracks (some short stretches a little overgrown but not scratchy) a few short sections on quiet lanes. Lots of fine & varied views, around this stunning location. Easy for the grade, only the accumulated height qualifies it
Directions: From south on CV-770 cross bridge & on hairpin bend at lower edge of village, turn R onto side road to car parks (signed) on R in about 200m. From north, as you leave village at hairpin turn L onto side road as above.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: A pleasant walk up to the ridge (twice) and around the west end of the mountain. An optional shorter route that goes to the ridge only once is also described.
Directions: Take the CV729 to Benimeli. In centre of Benimeli turn off the CV729 at brown sign “Pou de Baix”. Park near outdoor piscina.

Route Name: Ѧ Segaria West End from Rafol Ѧ
Route Description: A pleasant walk up to the ridge (twice) and around the west end of the mountain. An optional shorter route that goes to the ridge only once is also described.
Directions: From the N332 take the CV731 to Orba and Benidoleig. Turn R at the second island to Beniarbeig CV732. Go L immediately after the bridge onto the CV729 signed to Sagra. Ignore two RH turns to Sanet I Negrals and follow bypass to Benimeli. Go L at island, continue through Benimeli to Rafol. Turn first R, signed Centro Urban,(if approaching from Sagra itâ€™s the last turning L) first R again, over the bridge, R onto main road and immediately R again. Continue to end and R into the Rafol Dâ€™Almunia Centre Social (known as the Piscina bar) car park

Route Name: Ѧ Segaria western end from Monte Pego – extended Ѧ
Route Description: From the top of Monte Pego we walk to the ridge of Segaria where there is evidence of an Iberian settlement. We then drop down and around the western end of the mountain into Benimeli. We then return back to the ridge and retrace our steps back to the cars. All on well defined paths, tracks and quiet country roads. The shorter legged of our species may need a helping hand on occasion.
Directions: From the N332 take the CV700 in the direction of Pego. After approx 4 km turn L signed Monte Pego, then L again. (this turning is approx. 80m past the exit from Monte Pego which some find confusing!). Park in the first car park on the L just after the entrance to the urbanisation (restaurant on the R) The walk begins at the top of Monte Pego so we car share and drive up

Route Description: A circular walk following PRCV 155 on well marked, defined paths and forestry tracks. The route follows two high ridges and offers stunning scenery. Some of the inclines are steep and stoney
Directions: On entering Biar from Ibi on CV 799 the road turns sharply left then goes downhill passing the centres of commerce. At the bottom the road turns sharply right. Turn left here (there is a sign for â€œLa Coronaâ€ restaurant and supermarket Hiperber on the corner) Follow the road (Calle Navarra) until the asphalt stops and park on the levelled ground on the right

Route Name: Serra de Besa circuit from Alcalali (Summit optional)
Route Description: Pleasant paths, tracks & lanes to & back from the base of Serra de Besa. Steeply up the flank of a barranco. Then up over the low laying ridge, which is a little rough & scratchy in places (summit optional add 25min). Doubling back along its northern flank through beautiful woodland. Quite a tough walk for its grade!
Directions: From all directions. At the junction where the CV-750 from Jalon meets the & CV-720 Pedreguer to Parcent road. Small car park at junction & roadside parking opposite.

Route Name: Serrella circuit east returning via barranco de Les Foies
Route Description: A circular walk on Mozarabic trails broad forestry tracks and paths. Great views on a clear day.
Directions: Take the CV720 from Parcent and Benichembla to Castell de Castells. In the village, immediately opposite Hotel Serrella (on the RHS) turn L. After 20 m. turn L again into Calle Jose Antontio and them almost immediately L again down a ramp into the signed parking area.

Route Description: Original description too long. Must be amended to 400 characters or less. Please see WalksinSpain write up for current description.
Directions: Starting from Tarbena drive 0.5km up the road in the direction of Col de Rates to the crest of the hill and take the LH surfaced road to Castells. (CV-752). Drive a further 7km (in 2012 at Km. 7 sign) to a broad straight track going L. (S).Follow this main track for approx 5 km, passing the sign to Ajub del Xarquet on LHS. and continue as it zig zags up to the start. (Steep sections surfaced).Park where the road comes to a T junction. There is a signpost indicating Font dels Teixos 3.3 km.

Route Description: Over rolling hills to the north to gain and follow the ridge of Penyes Blanques to the summit. Returning via Senija Cross. Once out of the village the ascents though plentiful are never too steep. The views are varied and wide ranging.
Directions: From CV-745 at eastern end of village. Turn into Avinguda de les Corts Valenciana which by-passes centre. Park on road side near play area for small children, which has sub station next to it & road crossing opposite.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Sierra de Falconera Mollo de la Creu 1.
Route Description: A climb up this little known ridge initially steeply, beside a barranco to open views in all directions.
Directions: Meet in school car park. From Gandia bypass take the Barx / Gandia turn. At the roundabout turn sharp right before school and park there. There will be a restaurant meal afterwards.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Ѧ Mondúver from Parpalló Borrell Centre Ѧ
Route Description: Ascend icon Costa Blanca sumit with the aid of chains.

This walk varies from the 400m climb at the start followed by a clear but rough path along some 3km of steeply undulating cliff edge, (another 275m ascent and 350m descent), before returning to Albir along a variety of paths, tracks and roads through pinewoods entailing another 120m of ascent and 445m of descent to the start.
Â Similar to the ascent and descent involved in climbing the highest mountain in England! The return involves careful path finding, helped by a series of cairns and red dots and takes approx two hours.
Directions: Parking Faro de l'Albir. From Albir take the road which goes to the Lighthouse of Punta Albir & park in the ample car park at the barrier to vehicles.

Route Description: An excellent walk on well-defined tracks and paths with spectacular views from the summit and back down the ridge to Gata.
Directions: Approaching from the south on the N332 turn L into Calle Trossets 200m north from main intersection in Gata and park in street or in rough car park on the R. Approaching from the north on the N332 take the first R signed Xalo/Jalon into Calle Trossets. Walk starts from car park
Dogs: Dogs by prior arrangement with leader only

Route Name: Serra de Besa circuit (from CEIP Serra de Bernia)
Route Description: Circular walk from Jalon, mainly on narrow and sometimes rocky footpaths, on the pine-covered and deserted Serra de Besa, with beautiful views over the Val de Pop as we ascend.
Directions: From CV-750 in Jalon, turn into Camí del Cementeri (the road between the Cepsa petrol station and the Ferreteria Tot Util).  About 350m along Camí del Cementeri, on the left hand side, opposite the CEIP Serra de Bernia school, you will see a large gravel car park; park and meet here.
Restrictions: Not Wednesdays in term time; parking is in the school carpark and access is restricted.

Route Name: Tarbena circuit to Font d'Olbis and Castell dels Moros
Route Description: A circuit through the hills around Tarbena providing exquisite views and scenery all day. Considerable climb after lunch.
Directions: From CV715 Tarbena / Parcent road turn into car park near childrens' play area in Tarbena

Route Name: Tossalet del Castellet (El Cau) from Moli del Collao
Route Description:
A steeper short-cut to the Cau ridge by-passing construction work then a pleasant wide ridge walk to the summit returning down the southern slopes of El Cau overlooking Calpe and Penyal de Ifac.
A short section of the descent uses chains.
Directions: From Benissa towards Jalon on CV 750 turn left into the Moli del Collao urbanisation follow Partida Collao to the end. Park on wasteland on LHS just past Casa Alba.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Tollos circuit extended and in reverse
Route Description: A circular walk mainly on tracks, some quiet roads, and a short distance on a mozarabic path. Wonderful views.
Directions: Take the CV720 through Castell de Castells and past Famorca, Facheca and soon afterwards there is a turn to the right to the village of Tollos. Take this and just before reaching the village park on the right in the car park behind a small recreation area.

Route Description: Original description too long. Must be amended to 400 characters or less. Please see WalksinSpain write up for current description.
Directions: From La Nucia drive south along the CV70 towards Benidorm to Km.44. Immediately after the sign turn R and zero your odometer. Drive along the surfaced road with Montebello urbanization on your L and a new urbanization across the barranco on your R. for approx 0.9 km to reach a roundabout. Go straight across this roundabout and continue until reaching a Y junction. Take the right hand fork which is a track that is rough in parts, pass a Casa on your L with blue domed roofs and continue for a further 2.5km to where a track goes off down L to a ruin, a total of 3.4 km from the CV70. This junction is the start and there is parking for several cars. Note: After the blue Casa the track up to the start becomes very rough in places but is passable. If it proves too rough for your vehicle there are plenty of spots to pull off, park and walk the rest of the way to the start."

Route Name: Tossalet del Castellet (El Cau) anti clockwise
Route Description: A very pleasant ridge walk to the summit and return via barranco de les Cadiretes. Spectacular views of Jalon Valley and the coast.
Directions: Jalon to Benissa road, CV750, (km8) opposite Venta Roja Restaurante

Route Name: Eye of Montgo via Mont Putxol from Almacera resturant
Route Description: Taking in various points of interest. The route though a little convoluted is a nice way to approach the eye. Going via some Molins, a Civil War memorial & sections of woodland. Access into the interior of the cave requires scrambling but it is optional. Mainly good level paths though some are steep & have exposed views. Great scenery. Plus a very convenient cafe at the end.
Directions: From the CV-736 between Javea & Denia turn onto C' del Cap de Sant Antoni. In 400m turn R onto Cami Curt, immediately beside Restaurant Amanecer (it looks like their car park). Park at the rear at the side of the road.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at rear at all times

Route Description: An interesting walk over to Vall d'Ebo and back by a different route via Tossal Grau. Total walk on marked paths and tracks. Great views
Directions: Plaza del Metge Almela, above Pla de la Font, Paseo Cervantes Plaza.

Route Name: Vall d'Ebo circuit from Benimaurell reversed
Route Description: A testing walk partly over well established paths and tracks, some over less well established paths and animal tracks and about 2km “off-piste” over rocky terrain. Wonderful views from start to finish over sections of Sierras Caballo Verde and Carrasca.
Directions: On entering village take first right (Blue P sign) and follow road around edge of village in the direction of Alahuar Hotel. Large car park (The only one in the village) on right opposite Bar / Restaurante Jalisco

Route Description: Starts through Orba to the summit of Castell de Orba. The views from here are panoramic. Down to the col de Murla, into the Barranco de Fontilles. From Fontilles to Font de Isbert.Track descends to a turn through a tunnel of canes,now on good paths and tracks to El Polvorin, then passing Font Roja into the Girona river valley. Return via orange groves and Palmeria to the start.
Directions: Park and meet at the free carpark in Plaça Unidad Actuacion II, Orba.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at rear at all times

Route Name: Vall de Laguar - Los Cuatro Pueblos (Extended)
Route Description: A very pleasant walk that takes you to all 4 villages in the valley, namely: Fleix, Campell, Fontilles and Benimaurell. The extended section takes in the lower valley, a dam (Presa D'Isbert) and a tunnel (so bring along a torch). All on well-defined quite roads, tracks and paths through a mixed environment of agriculture and woodland.
Directions: Park opposite the school in the new car park in Fleix on the CV718.

Route Name: Vall de Laguar - Los Cuatro Pueblos
Route Description: A very pleasant walk that takes you to all 4 villages in the valley, namely: Fleix, Campell, Fontilles and Benimaurell. All on well-defined quite roads, tracks and paths through a mixed environment of agriculture and woodland.
Directions: Park opposite the school in the new car park in Fleix on the CV718.

Route Description: A varied circular walk through the “secret barranco” (aka the “dry waterfall”) ending in a challenging  climb. After lunch an interesting return around the flanks of Olta.
Directions: N332 south of Calpe Norte and Sur signs, km 166.6, just after Cala Mobel (closed furniture outlet) surfaced road on right, follow road 400m  - ample parking, but no left turn across N332 from Altea direction (best drive on to bar “Boca the Lupo” (1 km) for u-turn)!

Route Name: Alt de la Penya de Sella
Route Description: This little gem of a walk is relatively easy and gives access to a delightful high (1159m) summit and ridge, with spectacular 360deg views. Seen from Sella the mountain's impressive bulk looks daunting but, for those prepared to drive a little further the rewards are well worth it! Paths & tracks are straightforward & the limestone on the ridge is generally slabby and never too steep. But that said, the ridge element is rugged mountain walking.
Directions: From CV-770 at km 15.3 at eastern end of Sella on hairpin, turn into minor road to car parks (signed) on right in 200m. Meet here at 10am to arrange car sharing to the start. Which is at "Font Pouet Alemany". From Sella follow CV-770 NW to km 20.2 turn right at sharp bend onto minor road (at 38.62677, -0.29878) some potholes, after 7km arrive at font (limited parking). Walking starts from Font at 10.30am.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Circuit around the flanks of Benicadell
Route Description: A circuit across the lower slopes of the magnificent peak of Benicadell. Visiting caves with paintings (note; gates were locked at the time of writing) and a ruined castell. Mainly good easy paths though some are steep both up and down. Fine views over the countryside.
Directions: From CV-60 take CV-622. At roundabout at edge of Beniatjar. Turn 1st R into C' Cementerio and park at side of road.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at rear at all times

Route Name: Serra de Besa circuit (from Tourist Info Vall de Pop)
Route Description: Circular walk from Jalon, mainly on narrow and sometimes rocky footpaths, on the pine-covered and deserted Serra de Besa, with beautiful views over the Val de Pop as we ascend.
Directions: Park and meet by the Tourist Information Centre in Xaló / Jalón, opposite Casa Aleluya.
Restrictions: Not Saturdays; parking is impossible due to the rastro.

Route Name: Font d'Aixa valley & Castell d'Aixa Ridge
Route Description: The walk will take you through Lliber to the hidden valley, then towards Font d'Aixa before climbing the ridge above Pedreguer, returning to Lliber via Montanyeta. The walk will be on minor roads, tracks and good footpaths. Lovely views.
Directions: Approach Lliber from Jalon and turn left by the bridge just before the traffic lights at the start of Lliber village.Park down on the road adjacent to the riverbed.

Route Description: A varied route, which for the most part follows the PRCV-60. Taking in Fonts, a Hoyo, potholes, Neveretes, a summit with fine views and a Botanic micro reserve. After the initial flat valley track the route follows rugged mountain paths for the majority of the way, through a variety of Holly oaks, Cork Oaks & other species.
Directions: From Gandia on CV-675 at roundabout at eastern end of village with "BARX" sign on it. Take first exit onto Carrer Pep Andres Garba & turn R immediately & R again. Pass the Ajuntament De Barx office, turn R into car park. Opposite the roundabout.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: The full ascent is at the beginning of this walk taking 30 minutes. Then meandering downwards towards the outskirts of Pego and returning to Adsubia via terraced orange groves. 80% of this walk is on quiet country roads. Note later start time.
Directions: Follow CV 700 from Pego to Adsubia. Towards the end of the village turn left at Bar Moleta and park where convenient.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Tarbena - Segue - La Montana - Penya de Tarbena Circuit
Route Description: Not one but two summits! A Moorish castle, prehistoric settlement and wonderful views in every direction. A descent through the village leads across terraces and up the flanks of Segue (short steep section of hunters path, about 5mins) then a steady climb leads to the Castle & summit. Along an old mule path to stunning views of Paso Tancat then on to the summit of La Montana. Tracks & paths lead via a font back to the village, with more great views along the way. Mostly on good paths and tracks (some surfaced), with a few short rough sections of path.
Directions: From the north, take the CV715 from Parcent, over the Col de Rates and onwards to Tarbena. Pass the turning to Castell de Castells and at the outskirts of Tarbena on a bend continue straight ahead and uphill into Avenida Eusebio Signes. At the top of the rise turn right into the car park.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at rear at all times

Route Name: Serrella, Las Freginals ,Alto de Tronca and Pla de Blaconc
Route Description: A long steady ,early ascent on marked paths , descend down the ' canal 'to reach a ruin overlooking Guadalest embalse , pass a further ruin with well preserved ' era ' , then spiral downhill to Castell de Castells . Spectacular views and scenery throughout the route .
Directions: Take the CV720 from Parcent and Benichembla to Castell de Castells. In the village, immediately opposite Hotel Serrella (on the RHS) turn L. After 20 m. turn L again into Calle Jose Antontio and then almost immediately L again down a ramp into the signed parking area.

Route Name: Cabo de San Antonio to Windmills circuit
Route Description: Meet at end of road at light house for short walk across plana to windmills and back.Bring table and chairs if poss.Bring picnic i.e. wine beer food etc to share and enjoy letting in the new year with great scenery and Fun.
Directions: Denia to Javea /Javea to Denia mountain road take turn to Cap de sant Antoni light house.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: Easier walk on a mix of paths, forestry tracks, surfaced roads with good open views of the Jalon Valley and surrounding mountains. Also good views of Parcent and Alcalali.
Directions: Bar/Restaurante Piscina. From Parcent take CV715 (Rates to Tarbena road) for about 1 km. Car park on right.

Route Description: Woodland paths, tracks & quiet lanes lead to & from the small wooded ridge with its distinctive "Camels Humps". Where tracks & paths some steep, with the odd scrambling move both up & down, lead via Penya Roja (summit optional) then over the summits of & around the two "humps", which give wide ranging views.
Directions: From CV-738 at the edge of the village, turn into C' Pare Pere opposite the buildings of the Sabadell Solbank. Go up it past a square on the L into C' Major, turn first L into C' Atmtllers, then L at junction into C' Pinaret. Park on side of road or gravel car park on R.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Ѧ Cim del Penyalba via El Forat de la Drova Ѧ
Route Description: A circuitous undulating approach, via a cave to the "Forat de la Drova". An (optional) section of scrambling, then a fine open ridge with some scrambling moves & mild exposure over two tops. Very easy scrambling leads to the imposing summit with its crown of cliffs. Extensive 360 deg views. Descending the scrambling, regains part of the outward route. Virtually all on mountain paths, mostly well graded but sometimes steep and rocky!
Directions: From Gandia on CV-675 at roundabout at eastern end of village with "BARX" sign on it. Take first exit onto C' Pep Andres Garba and turn right immediately and right again. Pass the Ajutament De Barx office, then turn right into car park, which is opposite the roundabout!

Route Name: Les Foies to Punta de la Font Nova
Route Description: Passing through delightful scenery, to visit a natural font, a Forat and along a fine open ridge, to the summit of Punta de la Font Nova (750m). It has extensive 360deg views. Mostly on paths, some rugged & though steep never arduous. Despite the brevity & low height gain this is, in places, a rugged mountain route with a few awkward steps! There is also a scrambling option, which is quite exposed, should anyone fancy it! Though we intend to avoid it!
Directions: From Gandia on CV-675 at roundabout at eastern end of village with "BARX" sign on it. Take first exit onto C' Pep Andres Garba and turn right immediately and right again. Pass the Ajutament De Barx office, then turn right into car park, which is opposite the roundabout! From here we will car share, for the 12min drive to Font Nova at Les Foies.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: Cocoll starting and finishing from Benichembla on good gradient with stops to take in the views.
Directions: Bar Bon Aire, Benichembla on CV720 between Parcent and Castell de Castells

Route Name: Lower Bernia Circuit from Altea la Vella
Route Description: From the Font de Garroferet an ancient path leads us 600m up to the Paratge Font de Barca. the path offers wonderful views over the surrounding countryside. Once we are at the Paratge we follow a forrest road to the right to the Font del Rostol. Now we follow an other old path back down to the other side of Altea.
Pueblo: Altea la Vella / Altea la Vieja
Directions: Altea golf club. Coming from N332 or AP 7 take road to Altea La Vella. Take a right at the round about calle Principal to Altea club de Golf. Take a right at ave. de Bernia and enter P2 of the golfclub

Route Description: A circuit over the Alt de la Creu. Taking the way of the Borregos (sheep) and a section of mozarabic zig-zags then via ‘Font de la Sangonera’ to reach the summit, Mirador & principle Cross (there are two others). Descending via Fontetes Cantus’. Interesting terrain, with wide ranging views. Generally good marked paths, with some steep & rough sections.
Directions: From AP-7. Take CV-50 through town Pass the large brick library. Straight on at the roundabout, turn second right into ‘Carrer del Cantalot’. At far end of the road park at side just before a pylon.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at rear at all times

Route Description: Easy trail leading up to the pass (450m climb) before getting up a scrambling path to the castle. If you do not want to scamble you could have a long lunch at the pass. For the others it is an other 150 m up to the top. wW take a slightly different way back from the pass to later join the pass back to the village
Directions: Parking across the river below Bolulla

Route Name: Castell de Marinyen & Barranc de Cremades Circuit
Route Description: A visit to a font. Rugged paths through woodland. Steeply up stoney path to explore a moorish/christian castle ruin. Gradual ascent to a plateau and a mirador. Descent down a Mozarabic path with visit to a second mirador (optional). Mostly rugged rocky/stoney paths, some unmarked and a little overgrown in places but not scratchy. Varied terrain with splendid views. S/C if options are included.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at rear at all times

Route Name: Circuit of Barranc del Cau and Alt de Ample from Jalon
Route Description: The walk will take you up the path to the east of Barranc del Cau following the water pipe, circling around Les Planisses and returning via Alt de Ample. Generally the paths and tracks are good but there will be a short stretch over rough ground; the views are worth the effort!
Directions: From CV-750 in Jalon, turn into Camí del Cementeri (the road between the Cepsa petrol station and the Ferreteria Tot Util).  About 350m along Camí del Cementeri, on the left hand side, opposite the CEIP Serra de Bernia school, you will see a large gravel car park; park and meet here.  (If the school car park is full, there is an adjacent empty plot where you can park.)

Route Description: This is an adapted version of Charles Pye's Tres Barrancos walk. The route takes us up to the Bernia campsite and from there winds round and up to the Cau before returning via the L'Aspre barranco. Excellent views.
Directions: 1 km after Pinos restaurant on Benissa-Bernia road (CV749) take right hand junction just over bridge towards Marnes. Park after 200m.

Route Name: Barranco de la Canal and D'Alambra Castell (optional) – extended
Route Description: Small amount on roads but mainly on marked tracks and paths.
Directions: Meet at Xiringuito La Verdala in the Passeig Atzaneta where there is ample parking. (The Xiringuito is available for refreshments for early arrivals and at the completion of the walk.)

Route Name: Ѧ Carrascal de Parcent Ridge Circuit Ѧ
Route Description: Lovely walk starting with a 2 hour ascent. Great views on both sides along the ridge. The ridge is wide with an indistinct path in places but no exposure. Descent to Coll de Rates and back down to Parcent along the raisin trail.
Directions: Bar/Restaurante Piscina. From Parcent take CV715 (Rates to Tarbena road) for about 1 km. Car park on right.

Route Name: Ѧ Castell d'Aixa horseshoe from Pedreguer Ѧ
Route Description: Undulating walk, mainly on rocky paths with several tough ascents, one just before or after banana break, depending on the group, and one just before lunch.  **Please note 9.30am start instead of the usual 10.00am start. The earlier start enables us to get to Castle D'Aixa for lunch where we have beautiful panoramic views.**
Directions: Parking at Ermita sant blas. On CV720 Alcalali to Pedreguer road at Tourist signs to Ermita at edge of village, turn into Avenida de Maria Lopez and go to the far end of this road (over several junctions) and turn right to park near Ermita beside open ground.

Route Name: Beniali to Al Patro circuit via Pintures Rupestres
Route Description: A complex walk starting by visiting some excellent cave paintings and then with some sections with great views along the flanks on both sides of the Gallinera valley.
Directions: NEW CAR PARK. Follow the CV700 W from Pego and through Adsubia until you reach the KM45 marker (on LHS). Turn R (signed Parquing!) here down a small lane and curve around to the R at the bottom to find a large new village car park (signed).
Restrictions: good for cherry blossom – April?
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: A varied circular walk through the 'secret barranco' and an interesting return around the flanks of Olta.
Directions: N332 south of Calpe Norte and Sur signs, km 168.6 , surfaced road on right - ample parking, but no left turn across N332 from Altea direction !
Restrictions: Avoid Saturdays due to market in Calpe.

Route Name: El Cao (Llomo Larga) figure of Eight
Route Description: A long ascent to panoramic views of coast and mountains, cross the hemispheres, wind round and across Serra de Bernia then close the 'eight' on the eastern side of El Cau.
Directions: CV750 Benissa to Jalon road, approx.km 10. large surfaced layby - signpost also sign for El Collao restaurant.

Route Name: Ѧ Encimera de Cordilleras de Almadich Ѧ
Route Description: A circular walk with scenic views from the high level traverse above the Almadic valley. Incorporating some original paths of 'Dr Geoffs'
Directions: From CV720 Parcent to Benichembla at approx. Km. 36.8 (before Km 35) on an acute LH bend turn L beside a white wall onto a narrow surfaced road (with 10t sign) continue directly up for 200m and park near a small junction.

Route Name: Lliber Circuit, including the Hidden Valley and Font D'Aixa
Route Description: Good paths with great views, a short steep ascent up from Font d'Aixa up through the 'Squeeze' before lunch then downhill all the way back to Lliber.
Directions: Approach Lliber from Jalon and turn right by the traffic lights at the start of Lliber village. Meet in the car park behind the Medical Centre.
Restrictions: Avoid Saturdays

Route Description: This walk starts and ends with the Benichembla Stroll route but climbs rather than falls halfway to give splendid views, although we do go 'off piste' for a short steep climb.
Directions: Bar Bon Aire,Benichembla on CV720 between Parcent and Castell de Castells
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Montgo Denia X circuit from Los Lagos
Route Description: The walk starts from Los Largos where there is plenty of parking. A gentle ascent for 20 minutes through the wooded area behind Los Largos before reaching the gully. The gully is a steep climb of about 1 hour with sections of loose stones in places. Once at the top the walk continues with a gentle climb on good tracks. The final ascent becomes a little steeper on a very rocky path of the "pointy type” often experienced in this area. So sticks are a help. Spectacular views from the cross towards both Javea and Denia. Cameras a must. The descent initially follows the same rocky path down until it becomes a gentle descent on good paths. The final section is very scree like where again sticks would be a plus.Note this walk is very weather dependent as Montgó often has a “hat” even when the weather is good elsewhere. The walk may need to be modified if this is the case to miss the final ascent to the top.
Directions: Los Lagos. km 6 on CV735 between La Xara (near Denia) and Javea. Turn into Los Lagos, then immediately left and park.

Route Name: Ѧ Puig Campana long circuit clockwise Ѧ
Route Description: Clockwise circumnavigation of Puig Campana with a lunch next to a frog pond.
Directions: Enter Finestrat on CV761 from La Marina Shopping Centre, Benidorm (Carrefour) At T junction turn right onto CV 758 then after 300m take left turn to Font Molí. After 1km park in the carpark beyond the font.
Restrictions: Avoid Saturdays
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: A good walk with views over Benidorm to one side and Puig Campana to the other. Steep at the beginning to get onto the ridge, then undulating.
Directions: Take the cv-767 from either 332 or AP7 towards Finestrat about 2k before Finestrat at roundabout take first exit after 300m park on street"
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: Beautiful views from top.
Directions: Bar/Restaurante Piscina. From Parcent take CV715 (Rates to Tarbena road) for about 1 km. Car park on right.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Ѧ Segaria Western end from Monte Pego Ѧ
Route Description: From the top of Monte Pego we walk around the western end of the mountain down into Benimeli. We then climb to the mirador go down the other side and retrace our steps back to the cars. All on well defined paths, tracks and quiet country roads
Directions: From the N332 take the CV700 in the direction of Pego. After approx 4 km turn L signed Monte Pego, then L again. (this turning is approx. 80m past the exit from Monte Pego which some find confusing!). Park in the first car park on the L just after the entrance to the urbanisation (restaurant on the R) The walk begins at the top of Monte Pego so we car share and drive up

Route Name: Ѧ Tossalet del Castellet (El Cau) via western side of barranco del Cau below Alt de l’Ample Ѧ
Route Description: Circular route up the barranco Carretas, under Alt de Ample, up to El Cao and back down the “long ridge”(Loma Llarga).
Directions: Meet on slip road to Lady Elizabeth school approximately 300m east of Venta Roja restaurant on CV 750 Jalon - Benissa road
Restrictions: sat only to avoid parking problems

Route Description: A superb walk amongst high mountain scenery to a Col on the Serrella range before returning via a lower route. All on good tracks.
Directions: Take the CV-720 from Castells de Castells to Famorca. Take first L into village and drive to end and park by tennis/sports club.

Route Description: Ascend and pass through the Castellets with wonderful views, follow forest trails through the valley, another climb then return round the base of Puig Campana.
Directions: Enter Finestrat on CV761 from La Marina Shopping Centre .At roundabout turn R onto CV758 then after 300mtrs.take L turn to Font Moli and park just beyond Font to car share to start of walk.
Restrictions: Wednesdays only

Route Description: A circular clockwise route through forest tracks, visiting two summits, includes a scramble and wonderful views of Fontilles
Directions: Campell ( Val de Laguar ) Public car park on Cami de Fontilles , on CV721 Orba to Fleix direction turn L at P sign soon after Church and Bar in Campell.
Restrictions: Avoid Saturdays
Reservation notes: RESERVATION REQUIRED; WhatsApp leader to reserve place.

Route Description: A circular route with lots of ' ups and downs' well worth the exertion to appreciate the beautiful spring flowers.
Directions: Electric sub station /Jesus Pobre. CV738 Gata to Denia road
Restrictions: Wednesdays only; avoid weekends / fiestas due to hunters

Route Name: Col de Miserat and Travessia del Masset de Vall d'Ebo
Route Description: An interesting walk on marked paths, tracks and a little on quiet country roads. Spectacular descent back into Vall d'Ebo on Mozarabic path
Directions: From the CV-712 go over the bridge into Vall d'Ebo and and park at the edge of the village  Avinguda del Marina Alta). (There is also a car park behind Bar L'Entra.)
Restrictions: Avoid weekend of Festa Fira del Perelló (around 20th November)
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: Ascend steeply through a wood and eventually to Castell d’Aixa. From there on a good and scenic track towards Pedreguer. Return completes a clockwise circuit visiting Font d’Aixa.
Directions: Approach Lliber from Jalon and turn left by the bridge just before the traffic lights at the start of Lliber village.Park down on the road adjacent to the riverbed.

Route Name: Tormos circuit via Isbert’s Dam, Campell and Fontilles
Route Description: Leave Tormos on cart track to Isbert’s Dam from where we traverse through a tunnel (torches useful), climb on a mozarabic trail to Campell and then for a short while on tarmac (1km) past the camp site before re-joining a mozarabic trail descending towards Fontilles. There we cross the river, ascend briefly and then descend across the main mountain road and shortly return to the Infierno valley floor and back to Tormos.
Directions: Coming from the south (Orba) on the CV715 at the outskirts of the village turn L (signposted to Costera del Moll) into Calle Pozo. Take the next L (Carrer Val de Llaguart) and then take the 2nd turn on the RHS just after the bins. Drive to the end opposite a plaza and turn L into Avenguda Joan Carles I. Drive a few hundred metres along this and park in the large car park on the LHS opposite the public piscina.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at rear at all times

Route Name: Benimaurell via Colleen Corral Nou, Castellet de Garga, and El Coll de la Garda
Route Description: We accend to the ridge and then enjoy beautiful views walking along the ridge and return to village for lunch.
Directions: On entering village take first right (Blue P sign) and follow road around edge of village in the direction of Alahuar Hotel. Large car park (The only one in the village) on right opposite Bar / Restaurante Jalisco
Restrictions: Avoid Fiesta de Sant Antoni del Porquet (around 17th January) as Campell has pig roast which blocks off main street.

Route Name: Ѧ Malla de Llop Famorca Ѧ
Route Description: This iconic mountain is the second highest in the Serra de Serrella area. Although quite an initial strenuous ascent, there are no vertiginous parts. The views are superb with a Nevera adding further interest. The descent is via the "Canal" followed by a contouring lower route to the finish. Walking time is 4 hours, however the views and points of interest warrant 5/6 hours to complete the walk.
Directions: Take the CV-720 from Castells de Castells to Famorca. Take first L into village and drive to end and park by tennis/sports club.

Route Name: Serra de Besa & Penya Talai Summit
Route Description: Walk up Barranco Negro to Penya Talai summit for stunning views at lunch, then descending through the Vall de Pop back to Jalon.
Directions: Park and meet by the Tourist Information Centre in Xaló / Jalón, opposite Casa Aleluya.
Restrictions: Not Saturdays; parking is impossible due to the rastro.

Route Description: We descend to Font d'Isbert and take a circular route via Fontilles back. Beautiful views and mostly on good tracks.
Directions: Campbell – CV 721 km 5.3 Fleix Restaurant Cavall Verd. Drive through Campell from Orba on CV 721 towards Fleix, just outside Campell km5.3km turn left to restaurant Cavall Verd. Park up by the sports pitch.
Restrictions: Avoid Fiesta de Sant Antoni del Porquet (around 17th January) as Campell has pig roast which blocks off main street.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Ѧ Ponoch Summit and Carrasca Ѧ
Route Description: Ascent to summit of Ponoch using main path to avoid exposure & scramble. Ridge route will be available to the foolhardy. Return via barranco Carrasca & Buddhist retreat
Directions: Enter Finestrat on CV761 from La Marina Shopping Centre, Benidorm (Carrefour) At T junction turn right onto CV 758 then after 300m take left turn to Font Molí. After 1km park in the carpark after the font and wait for a convoy to the start of the walk.
Restrictions: Wednesdays only; avoid weekends / fiestas due to possibility of organised events

Route Name: Ѧ Aixorta from Bolulla Castle Ѧ
Route Description: A circular route to this stunning summit along mostly well defined paths - but the odd bit of cross country work for interest. Long ascents - but at a moderate pace.
Directions: Bolulla Castle. At Km 45.7 on Tarbena.Bolulla, CV 715, Road turn North and drive approx 3.5km to end of paved surface.

Route Name: Javea La Plana from the Port, return via Staircase
Route Description: From the port we go up to the lighthouse then along La Plana to the windmills and back down via the "Staircase". A delightful coastal walk with some fine views.
Directions: Meet at the fishing boat on Avenida del Port, at the north end of Avenida d'Ausias March, where there is ample on-street parking.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Javea La Plana from the Port, clockwise
Route Description: From the port we go up to the windmills and then along La Plana to the lighthouse, before descending to the port via the winding path of Cabo de San Antonio. A delightful coastal walk with some fine views.
Directions: Meet at the fishing boat on Avenida del Port, at the north end of Avenida d'Ausias March, where there is ample on-street parking.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: A short but interesting route, circumnavigating the “camel’s humps” of La Sella and then ascending to the high point of the Penya Budhista, and returning on wide tracks.  The ascent to the Penya Budhista includes a section of easy scrambling.  Far reaching views to the coast at Denia, and to the mountains of the interior of the Marina Alta.
Directions: From the N-332 take the CV-724 towards Denia and Pedreguer. Go over the first roundabout, and at the second roundabout take the first exit into the La Sella urbanisation.  At the next junction, bear right onto Av de l’Alacantí; meet by the recycling area on the right hand side, opposite the junction with Carrer de la Foia de Castalla.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: A gentle  walk through the woods to the river bed and return back through Lliber to Val Del Pop restaurant. Good paths, tracks and road.
Directions: Val de Pop restaurant, km 8.35, CV 748, Lliber to Gata road. ( from Lliber drive towards Senija, CV 745, and as you leave Lliber take the left turning CV 748 towards Gata, at Km 8.35, about 1 Km, the restaurant is signposted to the left by the post boxes and basuras, the large restaurant car park is 100m along this road on the left)
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Penyals Mica and Ampla and Barranco del Cao (Waterhouses)
Route Description: A forgotten summit, an old walk of Malcolm Blakeney, alternative route up Alt d'Ampla and return via newly cut Barranco del Cao includes an optional scramble.
Directions: Turn off CV750 Benissa /Jalon Road near fuel station in Jalon wind up and onto CV749 Jalon /Benissa Road at KM.1 park near animal corral on R.

Route Description: An intriguing walk under the craggy slopes of Aitana via several fonts, up an interesting rocky ramp and along its ridge before returning with fantastic views from the highest summit in the area.
Directions: Follow the CV70 from Benidorm / Polop direction towards Guadalest / Alcoy ,after Benimantell near to Km28 turn L (signed Benifato ) soon after turn up 2nd RH street ( sign for Fuente Partagat on wall ) continue up this steep minor road to arrive at the Fuente /Font

Route Name: Penya Roc/Mulero and flanks of Sanchet
Route Description: A tranquil walk with wonderful views of the Castellets and Aitana on forest and mountain trails
Directions: Polop/Guadalest rd. Km.33.5 turn L at sign for Trestellador Hotel then L at next smll.junction and park on layby

Route Description: A delightful round of the hills leading up to the Bernia with excellent views all around and down to the coast. Difficult later stage down a rocky slope and up a barranco with uphill finish back to the car.
Directions: From Jalon find the CV749 and follow this steadily uphill around all of its twists and turns to pass a large restaurant on the LHS and soon after some gravel parking on the RHS beside the 6km marker.
Restrictions: Weds Only

Route Name: Cabello verde ridge (west to east) - extended (the more difficult option)
Route Description: Mixture of animal tracks (narrow in places), some scrambling and ridge walk before descending back to Benimaurell
Directions: On entering village take first right (Blue P sign) and follow road around edge of village in the direction of Alahuar Hotel. Large car park (The only one on the village) on right opposite Bar / Restaurante Jalisco
Restrictions: Avoid Fiesta de Sant Antoni del Porquet (around 17th January) as Campell has pig roast which blocks off main street.

Route Description: An exploration through the woodland and valley around Forna with extensive views all around. We proceed thought the village to a footpath ascending thourgh th ewoods with occasional short steep sections. Then along though the woods, descending down  sometimes moderately steeply down to a barranco. Then along  to a road which ascends gently back to the village.
Directions: Arriving from Pego and through Adsubia take the RH turn on the CV717 to Forna.  Park in the car park on the outskirts of the village before reaching the narrow village roads.

Route Description: An easy canter down the valley from Forna towards the coast is followed by a challenging path ascent to the summit of the Puig. The walk along the ridge is rewarded by panoramic views in all directiona before descending into the woods and along to our return route over a rough path to Forna.
Directions: Arriving from Pego and through Adsubia take the RH turn on the CV717 to Forna.  Park in the car park on the outskirts of the village before reaching the narrow village roads.

Route Name: Ѧ Puig Campana Summit and circuit Ѧ
Route Description: Anti-Clockwise circumnavigation of Puig Campana with a side trip to the summit.
Directions: Enter Finestrat on CV761 from La Marina Shopping Centre, Benidorm (Carrefour) At T junction turn right onto CV 758 then after 300m take left turn to Font Molí. After 1km park in the carpark beyond the font.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Ѧ Malla de Llop - shortened. Ѧ
Route Description: A chance to enjoy this magnificent mountain on mostly good tracks with one short scramble and to view a well preserved nevera before returning to Famorca. A shorter route missing out the canal.
Directions: Take the CV-720 from Castells de Castells to Famorca. Take first L into village and drive to end and park by tennis/sports club.

Route Name: Ѧ Miserat summit de Adsubia Ѧ
Route Description: An interesting route mainly over tracks and paths (with a little on quiet country roads) and some "off piste", but not scratchy, to the summit. And what a view!
Directions: Follow CV700 from Pego to Adsubia. Towards the end of the village turn left at Bar Moleta and park where convenient.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: A circular route, a woodland path to a spectacular vista, a gully scramble to more panoramic views from the summit, down a barranco and return through more forest paths
Directions: CV 755 Altea to Callosa - at main roundabout in Callosa take 2nd. street on R (Avinguda Jaume 1 ) then R fork in front of Banco Santander, go up hill then L fork downhill - cross a junction and go up Calle Callosa d' Ensarria,continue for 2.7kms. on narrow tarmac road ( passing Urb. Almedia ), park near concrete casita. Sounds more complicated than it is !!!

Route Name: Calpe tennis club to Olta camp-site and back
Route Description: A figure of 8 walk through the countryside from Calpe up to the Olta camp-site, returning to the Tennis Club via the railway station and then continuing on varied tracks in the area with a stop for a picnic lunch. Those preferring a shorter walk can leave when we return to the Tennis Club. Stats for the shorter walk are 7k, 225m asc 2.5 hours.
Directions: Calpe tennis club (coming into Calpe from the N332, turn left at the Mas y Mas Centro Comercial roundabout and park by the tennis club or opposite).
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: Our route takes us on the north side of the Vall de Gallinera, all on marked paths and tracks and a stretch of country road in the middle section where you're not likely to see any vehicles. The wonderful views are well worth the effort.
Directions: Take CV700 from Pego through Adsubia until km45 marker (at LHS ) Turn R (signed Parquing ) down small lane to reach car park on RHS ( P )

Route Description: A splendid longer walk on well defined paths through attractive scenery. Steep climb before lunch then enjoyable high level stroll back. Great views especially after storming the castle
Directions: Parking at Ermita sant blas. On CV720 Alcalali to Pedreguer road at Tourist signs to Ermita at edge of village, turn into Avenida de Maria Lopez and go to the far end of this road (over several junctions) and turn right to park near Ermita beside open ground.

Route Description: Pleasant easy walk on good paths and quiet lanes passing Ermita Santa Barbara and Playa La Olla.
Directions: Meet Altea, large car park near Rio Algar. From Calpe, on approach to Altea pass traffic lights at Hotel Cap Negret, after 250 m. turn right by garden centre just BEFORE bridge over river. Follow road to left, turn right at stop sign, go under railway bridge, park immediately on left. From Benidorm, drive through Altea on N332 and turn left immediately AFTER bridge over river, then as above. From La Nucia, drive down CV760 to Altea, turn left at first small roundabout, left again at next roundabout, car park is on right at end of dual carriageway.

Route Description: Circular route, down through tunnel to Isberts Dam then climb steep shelf, on up for one hour approx to broad track and descend to river bed on dam side of the Barranco del Inferno and on up to Fleix.
Directions: Park opposite the school in the new car park in Fleix at km 5.9 on the CV721.

Route Description: The former Dos Hemisferos walk, recently resurrected. A mountaineer’s day out with a ridge route up the end of the Bernia and panoramic views all around. We cross and recross the Meridian several times in the day!
Directions: Follow the N332 S from Calpe and pass the entrance to the Maryvilla estate on the LHS. At km 165.7 there is a tarmac road on the RHS with signs to Ayuntamiento de Calpe construction project and also their Servicio de Proteccion and Recogido de Animales. Turn R up this road and follow it keeping as close to the motorway on the LHS as you are able. Once you go under the motorway, park where you can on the LHS verge.

Route Description: The first part of the walk is on Mozarabic paths, part of the dead dog walk, then on towards Planisses area for lunch. Continuing towards el Masserof, then onto rear of restaurant Verde Vent, completed by walking down the Barranc de la Cova on a good track. Note that this walk is at the top end of MS, but in the bracket as S as a precaution.
Directions: Take the Jalon to Bernia road, the CV749 and at approx. 2km, park on the left. Take care coming from Jalon because you will need to cross the road on a bend.

Route Name: Around Solana del Garrofer from Vall d'Ebo
Route Description: An interesting circular walk on tracks marked paths and some quiet country roads, all with nice views.
Directions: From the CV-712 go over the bridge into Vall d'Ebo and and park at the edge of the village  Avinguda del Marina Alta). (There is also a car park behind Bar L'Entra.)
Restrictions: Avoid weekend of Festa Fira del Perelló (around 20th November)
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Almond Blossom in Aspre - Bcos.Aspre ,Baron and Serra de Berna
Route Description: A circular trail through the Pinos valley and below the Bernia ridge
Directions: CV749 Benissa to Pinos road , park near a shrine opposite Pinos Restaurant.

Route Name: Ѧ Penya Roc Circuit and Summit Ѧ
Route Description: Enjoy some good forestry paths before reaching the ' scramble ' up a magnificent peak - 360deg.views rewards the exertion and a downhill return.
Directions: CV70 Polop/Guadalest road . Km 33.5 turn L at sign for Trestellador Hotel , then soon after turn L at next small junction after approx.200mtrs park on layby

Route Description: A winding ascent leads upwards to these impressive rock pinnacles ' Els Frares ' then onto the ridge and return down the valley below Pla de la Casa
Directions: In Facheca take L turn signed Quatretondeta ,CV754 ,almost immediately turn L and follow up to end of surfaced road and park near a ruin.

Route Description: Although graded MS this is a demanding walk with some exposed scrambling near the end of the day. Nevertheless it visits some exquisite scenery in a remote barranco with fascinating rock sculptured bed
Directions: From the CV-712 go over the bridge into Vall d'Ebo and and park at the edge of the village  Avinguda del Marina Alta). (There is also a car park behind Bar L'Entra.)
Restrictions: Avoid weekend of Festa Fira del Perelló (around 20th November)

Route Description: An old Eric Wright with a ' little extra ' - a country walk with lanes,footpaths a barranco through a deeply eroded valley with sweeping views.
Directions: CV720 Castell de Castelles to Facheca , turn onto CV754 Quatrotondeta and soon after park near Bar Facheca opposite play area

Route Name: Barranco d'Almadic valley circuit returning via Barranco del Bou
Route Description: Gentle ascent on good tracks and paths (a little awkward underfoot towards end of ascent), traverse back around the mountainside to join a Y/W marked track back to the village.
Directions: Bar Bon Aire, Benichembla on CV720 between Parcent and Castell de Castells
Dogs: Dogs on lead at rear at all times

Route Description: A circular walk combining parts of Foyes Valley, Castells South & East Circuits and the foothills of Aixorta. A mixture of broad forestry tracks, marked paths, mozarabic paths and a few rough tracks.
Directions: Take the CV720 from Parcent and Benichembla to Castells de Castells. In the village, immediately opposite Hotel Serella (on RHS) turn L. After 20m, turn L again into Calle Jose Antonio and then almost immediately L again down a ramp into the signed parking area.

Route Description: An attractive walk, with different climbing over bedrock as well as interesting features, over the summit of Menejador 1,352m. Walk commences at 750m PR-CV 26.
Directions: From centre of Ibi/Ajuntament take CV801 towards Banyeres and Font Roca for 700m to the exit sign for Ibi. Park on wasteland opposite large factory.

Route Description: Quiet lanes, old town and sea front.
Directions: Opposite Restaurante El Patio. From Calpe drive along the N332 through the centre of Altea; after passing the main tram station on the right, get in the right-hand lane to turn left (sign Cap Blanch) at the next traffic lights. At the sea front turn left and then sharp right (1st exit) at the small roundabout to enter the parking area (which is an easy walk from Altea tram station).

Route Description: Over and around rural tracks and paths yielding great views of the surrounding mountains without need to climb a peak.
Directions: As you enter the village from the Benichembla direction on the CV720, take the 2nd left signed for the cemetery immediately follow the road round to the left and proceed about 200m to the car park

Route Name: Barranco de la Encantada via Ermita de Santo Cristo circuit
Route Description: Very pretty circuit through part of the Barranco de la Encantada, returning via the Ermito de Santo Cristo, near to Planes.
Directions: On the CV700 between Pego and Muro de Alcoy, around the 29k marker look for road signs pointing to the Barranc de l'Encantada. Turn right down Cami de la Encanta. There is a newly created parking area about 100 metres on the right.

Route Description: This circular walk has spectacular views . We also return to the Little Rock Arch and a traverse along the northern slopes of Aixorta. Both arches are geological curiosities and probably formed by a harder part of the roof of a cave the remainder of which has fallen in.
Directions: Coming from Castell de Castells on the CV752. Eventually reach an unsurfaced road and walk sign on the right near the Km 7 post and turn right and park here. This is the start and finish point.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Forada Ridge from Alcala de la Jovada
Route Description: A pleasant walk with splendid views around the Gallinera valley. This gently undulating walk takes in the Forada ridge, a nevera, a cave house and an old abandoned Moorish village.
Directions: From the Orba to Pego road near Pego take the CV712 signed to Vall d’Ebo. Continue past Vall d’Ebo to Alcada de la Jovada and park on edge of village near the swimming pool.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: Start Adsubia, walk up to castle, then Benirrama, then on up mozarabic path to the ridge for lunch, then round back side of Miserat and back down frying pan handle to bar!
Directions: Follow CV700 from Pego to Adsubia. Towards the end of the village turn left at Bar Moleta and park where convenient.

Route Description: Heading up single track through cactus beds, then at top of this long single track swinging left on obscure old tracks with views to Almadich. Down towards the valley bottom then up left on single track all the way to El Mirabo for lunch. Then back down single track to cactus beds and the bar!
Directions: New location of the start and parking: On entering Benichembla from Parcent, on CV 720, Car Park on LHS, 100m before Bar Bon Aire. Turn left into Carrer de la Foia then immediate right into Car Park
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: Leaving Benimaurell the walk ascends to and along the Cabello Verde Ridge, then around the head of the Vall de Laguar. The walk then descends into the Barranc dels Racons then ascends out of the Barranc to return to the start.
Directions: On entering village take first right (Blue P sign) and follow road around edge of village in the direction of Alahuar Hotel. Large car park (The only one in the village) on right opposite Bar / Restaurante Jalisco
Restrictions: Avoid Fiesta de Sant Antoni del Porquet (around 17th January) as Campell has pig roast which blocks off main street.

Route Name: Ѧ Clockwise Miserat summit Ѧ from Benirrama
Route Description: Majority on well-defined paths, tracks and a small amount on quiet country roads circling 13th C Benirrama Castle and the northern lower slopes of El Miserat. The final route to the summit is from the south on a marked path returning from the summit via the road and then gently downhill on an excellent mozarabic path back into Benirrama.
Directions: Take CV-700 from Pego, direction Planes, past L’Atzubia and turn left to Benirrama village (CV-7170) at km 46.5. Turn right as you enter the village up a narrow road to the parking area.
Restrictions: Avoid weekends / fiestas due to parking restrictions / difficulties
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Sierra del Sireret from Alcala de la Jovada
Route Description: A circular walk mainly on wide tracks and clear paths. The route along the ridge, which is optional, is "off piste".
Directions: From the Orba to Pego road near Pego take the CV712 signed to Vall d’Ebo. Continue past Vall d’Ebo to Alcala de la Jovada and park on the furthest edge of village near the public swimming pool.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: A circuit over Solana del Garrofer.
Route Description: A rewarding walk mainly on marked or well used paths and a little on a quiet country road. There is a little “off-piste” but this is good underfoot and not scratchy. A must for the views.
Directions: From the CV-712 go over the bridge into Vall d'Ebo and and park at the edge of the village  Avinguda del Marina Alta). (There is also a car park behind Bar L'Entra.)
Restrictions: Avoid weekend of Festa Fira del Perelló (around 20th November)
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: A bit of everything, splendid mozarabic path at the beginning, "off piste" too, along and down from the ridge and a stroll back. And the views …
Directions: On entering village take first right (Blue P sign) and follow road around edge of village in the direction of Alahuar Hotel. Large car park (The only one in the village) on right opposite Bar / Restaurante Jalisco
Restrictions: Avoid Fiesta de Sant Antoni del Porquet (around 17th January) as Campell has pig roast which blocks off main street.

Route Name: Ѧ Forada ridge - extended from Alcada de la Jovada Ѧ
Route Description: A pleasant walk with splendid views of the Gallinera valley
Directions: From the Orba to Pego road near Pego take the CV712 signed to Vall d’Ebo. Continue past Vall d’Ebo to Alcala de la Jovada and park on the furthest edge of village near the public swimming pool (swimming).
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: Spectacular views from this popular ridge ,then descend down a reopened path , visit 2 Fonts , pass 2 ruins before ascending to reach and scramble up the rock strewn Arechinos and return across scrubland to the cars.
Directions: Collado de Garga
Restrictions: Avoid Fiesta de Sant Antoni del Porquet (around 17th January) as Campell has pig roast which blocks off main street.

Route Description: A tough alternative ascent to this iconic summit, up, up and up for some spectacular views, scramble down and follow an interesting animal path to the Sanchet circuit and return through a forest trail. This is a demanding route. Please check with the leader in advance if unsure about your ability to participate.
Directions: From main roundabout in Polop take exit on CV715 signed La Nucia, continue up to meet roundabout on CV70 and take exit Avd. Balco de Ponoig follow up towards base of Ponoch and park on large car park nearwater depositer/ helipad

Route Name: El Penyot, Sierra de Venta, Maserof
Route Description: Climb up a newly cut gully - across easy hills with extensive views of the surrounding mountains then return down an interesting barranco.
Directions: Take the Jalon to Bernia road, the CV749 and at approx. 2km, park on the left. Take care coming from Jalon because you will need to cross the road on a bend.
Reservation notes: RESERVATION REQUIRED; WhatsApp leader to reserve place.

Route Description: A beautiful walk through some of the Algar valley , a long ascent upto the Carrascal ridge and enjoy the impressive scenery on the return route. This is a demanding route. Please check with the leader in advance if unsure about your ability to participate.
Directions: From CV715 Tarbena / Parcent road turn into car park near childrens' play area in Tarbena

Route Description: Small amount on roads but mainly on good marked tracks and paths albeit a short stretch of path is a little rocky underfoot. Lovely views, particularly from the castle
Directions: Plaza del Metge Almela, above Pla de la Font, Paseo Cervantes Plaza.

Route Description: A walk around Montnegre from the village of Vall d'Ebo. Wonderful views down to the coast and the Pego valley before returning on a steep Mozarabic path back to Vall d' Ebo.
Directions: From the CV-712 go over the bridge into Vall d'Ebo and and park at the edge of the village  Avinguda del Marina Alta). (There is also a car park behind Bar L'Entra.)
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Lliber circuit from Val del Pop restaurant
Route Description: We walk around the hillside, initially above Lliber, before descending to the river bed and returning via the “hidden valley”
Directions: Val de Pop restaurant (now closed) , km 8.35, CV 748, Lliber to Gata road. From Lliber drive towards Senija, CV 745, and as you leave Lliber take the left turning CV 748 towards Gata, at Km 8.35, about 1 Km, there is a cross roads, turn left by the post boxes and basuras and park along this road (the restaurant car park may be open, 100m on the left)
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: A circular stroll around Lliber, almost all good tracks.
Directions: Lliber square next to church. Lliber. Village is in Jalon Valley on CV 750 between Senija and Jalon
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Albir to Benidorm beach via Sierra Helada
Route Description: Stiff climb out of Albir then undulations to Benidorm with stunning views. One descent is steep and scrambly. There will be banana and photo stops but no lunch break. At Benidorm we will walk along the beach for a short distance to the Chinese for lunch. Number 10 bus will take us back to Albir and the cars.
Directions: Park in car park behind “Consum” supermarket in centre of Albir on right-hand side of road from N332 (McDonald’s crossing) and the beach. After parking cross the road in front of Consum and meet at the cafe Malibu where the coffee is good.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times
Lunch_break notes: Optional lunch at chinese restaurant in Benidorm.

Route Name: Circuit to Cova Blanca anti clockwise
Route Description: A circuit walk around the Barranco de la Canal on roads, well defined paths, rough tracks and one short steep ascent where hands will be helpful.
Directions: Meet at Xiringuito La Verdala in the Passage Atzaneto where there is ample parking. (The Xiringuito is available for refreshments for early arrivals and at the completion of the walk.)

Route Description: Awaiting description from leader
Directions: Bar Bon Aire, Benichembla on CV720 between Parcent and Castell de Castells
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Tormos easy circuit via Isbert's dam.
Route Description: A pleasant afternoon stroll or pre-lunch appetizer in dramatic countryside.
Directions: Coming from the south (Orba) on the CV715 at the outskirts of the village turn L (signposted to Costera del Moll) into Calle Pozo. Take the next L (Carrer Val de Llaguart) and then take the 2nd turn on the RHS just after the bins. Drive to the end opposite a plaza and turn L into Avenguda Joan Carles I. Drive a few hundred metres along this and park in the large car park on the LHS opposite the public piscina.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at rear at all times

Route Name: Villages of the Vall de Laguar from Murla Polideportivo
Route Description: After first trecking up to the foothills of Caballo Verde Ridge, we walk on to Benimaurell, then Fleix, and Campell before passing through Fontilles, then back to Murla. Some road walking.
Directions: Murla Polideportiu. Approaching Murla from East on the CV719, turn right on outskirts of village (signed). Large sports centre on LHS after about 1 km.

Route Name: Jalon Parcent circuit via Coll de Rates extended
Route Description: Route mainly on tracks, some country roads, and mainly marked paths. Magnificent views from the col and a wonderful return when the almond blossom is in bloom.
Directions: In Jalon take the cemetery road that runs between the petrol station and the Ferreteria, Cami del Cementeri. The parking is a few hundred metres along this road on the RHS.
Restrictions: Avoid Saturdays if possible because parking is difficult with Jalon Rastro.

Route Name: Ѧ Ponoch summit and Sanchet circuitѦ
Route Description: An alternative route up to this iconic summit ,scramble up and enjoy the panoramic views along the ridge ,wind down to continue round the Sanchet circuit then return through a forest path.
Directions: Polop Helipad. From main roundabout in Polop take exit on CV715 signed La Nucia, continue up to meet roundabout on CV70 and take exit Avd. Balco de Ponoig follow up towards base of Ponoch and park on large car park nearwater depositer/ helipad

Route Description: A mixture of new and old paths and trails around this popular area with extensive views along the route.
Directions: From the N332 at its junction with the AP7, take the slip road towards the motorway and before reaching the toll gates take a R turn onto a minor road that runs alongside the access road - signed to the Cementeri. 650m later turn R - still signed Cementeri. 350m after this ignore the R turn to the Cementeri and continue directly ahead to arrive after a further 1.3km at a sharp LH bend by the electricity sub-station. Park here. "
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: An early ascent up an old winding hunters path leads to Alfaro summit, then head down towards Malafi and wind along through Tollos, bypass Benimassot and follow a forest trail to Facheca then a country path to return to cars in Famorca.
Directions: Take the CV-720 from Castells de Castells to Famorca. Take first L into village and drive to end and park by tennis/sports club.

Route Name: Azafor/La Safor, L'Orxa, Riu Serpis circuit
Route Description: A challenging, interesting and varied walk including a Nevera, woodland paths, a font, a cave, an historic bridge, a castle, a beautiful gorge, old railway tunnels, a waterfall, extensive views and tranquil riverside.
Directions: Villalonga - Via Pista/ Reprimala

Route Description: A circular walk all on good paths and broad forestry tracks. Stunning views on a clear day especially from the castle.
Directions: Take the CV720 from Parcent and Benichembla to Castell de Castells. In the village, immediately opposite Hotel Serrella (on the RHS) turn L. After 20 m. turn L again into Calle Jose Antontio and them almost immediately L again down a ramp into the signed parking area.

Route Description: A series of loops to explore the Abdet valley with lunch on a ridge overlooking the Guadalest Valley. Lots of good tracks, a few steams to cross and spectacular scenery. A Kees Andriessen walk
Directions: At Km 24.3, just East of Confrides, Turn off CV 70 on CV 7560 towards Abdet. After 1km Turn left and after a further 100 m keep left again (opposite rubbish containers). Follow road up for 1.35 km to start of walk.
Restrictions: Avoid Saturdays
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Beniali Circuit to La Carrotxa via Pintures Rupestres
Route Description: A walk that explores the valley sides to gain good views of the Gallinera villages. The walk starts with a short loop walk to take in the ancient cave paintings.
Directions: NEW CAR PARK. Follow the CV700 W from Pego and through Adsubia until you reach the KM45 marker (on LHS). Turn R (signed Parquing!) here down a small lane and curve around to the R at the bottom to find a large new village car park (signed).
Restrictions: Good for cherry blossom in April?
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Serella castle and Aixorta flanks from Castell de Castells
Route Description: A steep walk out of the village up to the castle on good tracks and paths. There is then an optional scramble up to castle to gain the excellent views down to Guadalest and beyond. We then follow the ridge on paths but with a short section of 'off piste'. The gentle descent takes us around les arcs and then returning to Castell via the Foies valley.
Directions: Take the CV720 through Pedreguer and Parcent to reach the village of Castells. On entering the village the car park is on the L at a T-jnc. Turn into calle Jose Antonion and drop down a ramp into the car park.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: This is a walk on good tracks and paths. It starts fairly steeply uphill but after that it meanders gently up to the head of the valley with great views down to Castells. Our route passes Font de la Retura a very pleasant spot before crossing the CV752 to reach an interesting ruin which is bound to cause discussion. Although at the top end of the ‘M’ grade after the initial climb it is easy and good going.
Directions: Take CV720 through Benigembla to Castell de Castells. On entering the village continue  past Hotel Serrella on R, further on there are 2 new parking  areas, park in the second one
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Description: This is a popular walk and deservedly so. It is a circuit encompassing the main part of the Sierra but excluding its Eastern end. Starting at an altitude of 650 meters gets you into easy contact with the higher part of the mountain. Yet the walk is quite challenging involving some easy short rock scrambles, short traverses across or slightly up scree, some steep climbs and a 30-meter long semi stoop/ crawl through the \"Forat\". Views are magnificent especially from the Fort onwards. The ruined Fort is interesting and the \"Forat” is a curious feature. This is a tunnel through the \"rock spine\" of the Sierra some 30 meters long and in part approx a meter high and wide, not claustrophobic as daylight shines through and taken with care, no hazards. Sometimes muddy.
Pueblo: Altea la Vella / Altea la Vieja
Directions: The start is at the Bernia Barbecue car park high up a steep badly surfaced road above Altea La Vieja. Starting from the Village of Altea La Vieja take the CV755 towards Callosa. Pass the RH turns to Alhama and Paradiso and pass a casa on the RHS with a large statue. Go slow along the straight stretch and take the next rather obscure RH turn, signposted Fort Bernia, (just before Km. 19). (If you miss this take the next RH turn which also leads up). Follow this narrow twisting road steep up some 6 km to its end at the Barbecue car park (BBQ). NOT FOR NERVOUS DRIVERS.

Route Description: Starting from the car park in the village, leave the carpark up the ramp and turn R. Proceed straight ahead down the narrow street. Continue along the road and bear L down the small hill and past the font. Proceed over the bridge and up to the road. Turn L and after 50m turn R up the concrete road signed to the castle and the campground. Time and distance start from the concrete road.
Directions: Take the CV720 from Parcent and Benichembla to Castell de Castells. In the village, immediately opposite Hotel Serrella (on the RHS) turn L. After 20 m. turn L again into Calle Jose Antontio and then almost immediately L again down a ramp into the signed parking area.

Route Description: Varied walk almost all on forestry tracks with short riverbed stretch and one mozarabic path.
Directions: From the centere crossroads in Finestrat drive N to Font Moli. From here continue along the “main” surfaced road 3.4 km to a junction with a surfaced road going up R. This is the start and has parking for at least 4 cars. (N.B. More roads are being surfaced in this area).

Route Description: RV 112 Font de Vivens is a picnic site, reached by climbing up a barranco, returning down a different barranco. Y/W marked all the way.
Directions: Leave Jijona towards Tibi on CV810. approx 0.7 km after traffic lights for narrow road,on a sharp left hand bend turn right into Calle Ibi. Y/W on lamppost and signs to Fonts. Follow road around to the L and Park outside the factory (Jijona SA) at the end of the road.

Route Description: A fairly long circular walk starting with a steep climb on good paths up the Barranco de Galabdar below the escarpments of Sanxet. Then heads west levelling out until the short but impressive zigzag up the Passet de Golers. Here there is a rocky lookout which makes an ideal lunch stop. Another steep climb to reach the peaceful Arc Valley and the Paso Contador with spectacular views. From here it is downhill (steeply in places) all the way back to the previously spotted car, which will be used to ferry drivers up the hill to the Casa de Dios. Although this walk can be easily walked as a complete circuit we shorten it, whenever possible, by spotting a car which avoids an uphill walk on a surfaced road. 57% Paths, 43% Tracks.
Directions: From La Nucia take the CV70 towards Guadalest and Benimantell. Go to the KM38 sign continue a further 0.7km and turn sharp left up a concrete surfaced road. Drive approx 2.7kms to a junction with a chained track going up right. (Our return route). Spot a car here if possible. Continue up the road for approx. 2km. and park by the Casa de Dios (Painted Blue in 2011).

Route Description: A pleasant wander on the flanks of the mountains and through orchards. This walk has a 40 minute steady climb. Not steep,but be prepared.
Directions: From Pego follow the CV700 to Adsubia. Drive through the village to find Bar Moleta on the LHS and turn down the street beside it. Either park here or if this is full go down the hill, turn R and park where you can.
Dogs: Dogs on lead at all times

Route Name: Ѧ Cabeco d'Or circuit and optional summit Ѧ
Route Description: A stunning tour of this impressive mountain on very good tracks with a side trip to the summit which involves some scrambling and a steep ascent/descent to the top.
